sources.title: Honduras Migration: Climate Change, Violence, & Assistance
sources.temporal_coverage: Retain the dated scope of individual claims; no extrapolation to present conditions.
sources.methodology: Department-level models link 2012–2019 US family apprehensions, birthplace, rainfall deviations and homicide rates.
sources.limitations: Birthplace is not necessarily departure residence; observational associations, not causal attribution.

sources.title: Encuesta de Hogares: Vulnerabilidad y Sequía, Corredor Seco Honduras 2021
sources.temporal_coverage: Retain the dated scope of individual claims; no extrapolation to present conditions.
sources.methodology: January 2021 survey of 713 households in 12 selected drought-affected communities; systematic household sample within selected sites.
sources.limitations: Municipalities/sites were selected for drought and migration/access criteria; not nationally representative.

sources.title: La paradoja del sur de Honduras: riqueza geoestratégica y deuda social en Choluteca y Valle
sources.temporal_coverage: Retain the dated scope of individual claims; no extrapolation to present conditions.
sources.methodology: Regional analysis combines secondary information with August 2025 community-leader discussions.
sources.limitations: Reports community concerns and allegations, not adjudicated hydrological or legal findings.

sources.title: Honduras country strategic plan 2023–2027
sources.temporal_coverage: Retain the dated scope of individual claims; no extrapolation to present conditions.
sources.methodology: Substantive publisher summary of approved plan; page records December 2024 revision.
sources.limitations: Priorities and intended outcomes are not delivery or impact evidence.

claims.locator: Physical PDF pp.1–4, methods and interaction models.
claims.paraphrase: Rainfall deficits were associated with more subsequent US family-unit apprehensions from Honduran departments in 2012–2019; the relationship was stronger where homicide rates were higher.
claims.limitations: Departmental association, not climate-caused violence or individual migration causality.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The observed rainfall-deficit/apprehension association was stronger under higher department homicide rates.

claims.paraphrase: The authors interpret intertwined weather/livelihood stress and violence as potentially limiting safe internal alternatives before cross-border movement.
claims.limitations: Interpretation, not direct measurement of each household’s options.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The brief interprets violence as potentially narrowing safe internal alternatives during livelihood stress.

claims.locator: Physical PDF pp.1 and 5, policy recommendations.
claims.paraphrase: The brief proposes local farmer participation in agricultural investment alongside responses to governance and violence, rather than assuming aid alone resolves migration pressures.

claims.locator: Physical PDF p.18 (printed p.18), drought section.
claims.paraphrase: In Pespire, San Lorenzo and El Corpus study communities, surveyed households reported drought-linked food-price and water/health burdens and livelihood interruptions; reduced food intake and savings use were common coping responses.
claims.limitations: Selected-community self-reports, not current national estimates.

claims.paraphrase: Among surveyed agricultural workers, roughly two-thirds worked third-party land; women aged 18–29 had the highest unemployment, indicating differentiated livelihood constraints.
claims.limitations: Separate survey indicators, not a demonstrated gender–tenure interaction.

claims.locator: Physical PDF p.17, definition and footnote.
claims.paraphrase: The survey’s “forced internal migration” category explicitly includes moves for work; its results must not be equated with standard conflict/disaster displacement counts.

claims.locator: Physical PDF p.14, water and agrarian conflicts.
claims.paraphrase: Leaders reported irrigation-related water-access tensions around Namasigüe and Choluteca and concern in Caridad/Alianza over proposed upstream Goascorán impoundment.
claims.limitations: Community concerns; no verified flow reduction or climate-attributable violence.

claims.paraphrase: The analysis reports restricted traditional fishing access at Amapala beaches and mangrove-loss concerns in San Lorenzo, alongside Cedeño coastal vulnerability.
claims.limitations: Reported context, not an attributed erosion or violence estimate.

claims.paraphrase: The report identifies Goascorán’s binational water/adaptation cooperation as an existing capacity, while noting deforestation and intensive land-use pressures.
WFP’s plan commits to gender-sensitive shock-responsive social protection, stronger national/local partners, healthier masculinities and GBV reduction.
claims.limitations: Planned approach through 2027, not demonstrated protection gains.

claims.paraphrase: The plan describes crime, inequality and climate variability as joint constraints on humanitarian and longer-term initiatives, especially affecting women, Indigenous and Afro-descendant groups.
claims.limitations: National diagnosis, not a named adaptation project blocked by violence.

search_audit.query: Honduras climate risk vulnerability Choluteca Valle women indigenous adaptation report 2024
search_audit.outcome: Inspected IOM selected-community drought survey and CESPAD regional report; retained local scope and methods.

search_audit.query: Honduras migration climate change violence assistance Bermeo Leblang 2021 Duke pdf
search_audit.outcome: Read original Duke brief and interaction-model interpretation; associations kept separate from causal estimates.

search_audit.query: Honduras insecurity humanitarian access climate adaptation flood recovery evaluation WFP
search_audit.outcome: WFP plan supplies national constraints, not a named evaluated adaptation failure; USAID and IOM crisis-plan original bodies inaccessible and excluded.

search_audit.query: Honduras drought violence climate local resilience evaluation WFP Dry Corridor 2025 pdf
search_audit.outcome: Retained WFP plan commitments and Goascorán cooperation without claiming effectiveness.

gaps: Duke models use birthplace, not necessarily residence before departure, and apprehensions rather than all migration; no causal estimate of rainfall causing violence is established.
CESPAD reflects local political-economy perspectives and reported concerns; no water-flow audit or legal adjudication was inspected.
USAID PDF host failed DNS; IOM crisis-response-plan body and the 2026 journal article returned access errors. Indexed text from them is not used.
No inspected source independently evaluates local climate–peace outcomes or establishes current safe routes.
